summary: A switch for an on/off setting, with its label, description and error laid out beside it, taking part in forms.

label.note: Visible label next to the track and accessible name. Required: shadow DOM keeps external <label for> from reaching the inner input.

hideLabel.note: Visually hides the label; it stays the accessible name. Use only when the row has other visible text naming the switch.

error.note: Error message. Setting it marks the field invalid.

value.note: Submitted with the form while on.

checked.note: On state. Not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset.

required.note: Native required: must be on. Adds an aria-hidden asterisk after the label.

disabled.note: Native disabled; dimmed; not submitted. Also set by a disabled fieldset ancestor without touching the attribute.

anatomy.name: field
anatomy.notes: Grid: track in the first column, label, description and error in the second.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: Track wrapper; holds the native input stretched over it.

anatomy.name: input
anatomy.notes: Native <input type="checkbox" role="switch">, visually the track; receives focus, Space and validation.

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: Sliding knob, drawn from the input's :checked state; aria-hidden, no pointer events.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: Native <label for> in the same shadow root.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Persistent polite live region; text appears when invalid.

input.note: Each toggle. Native and composed, so it crosses the shadow boundary.

change.note: Toggle committed. Re-dispatched from the host because native change is not composed (NativeControl).

focus-visible.note: 3px solid ring in ring color (a translucent ring would fall under 3:1).

checked.note: Track fills with primary and the thumb slides to the end (the opposite side in RTL).

invalid.trigger: error set, or required and off after blur or a submit attempt

disabled.trigger: disabled attribute or a disabled fieldset ancestor

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop, through a native <label for> in the same shadow root.

formAssociation.note: ElementInternals through FormAssociated: setFormValue(value) only while on, validity mirrored from the inner input (required -> valueMissing, error -> customError), formResetCallback restores the default checked attribute, disabled (own or fieldset) is not submitted, formStateRestore restores the saved on/off state.

accessibility.targetSize: Track is 32x20px (24x16px in sm), under 24px high; the whole field row (label included) is the click target and its min height is 24px, which meets WCAG 2.5.8.
accessibility.focusRingVisible: On keyboard focus of the input; 3px ring in switch.focus-ring.color.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Dev-only console warning, once, when label is empty.

keyboard.Tab: move focus to and from the switch
keyboard.Enter: submits the form (implicit submission; the control has no form owner in its shadow root, SB-0009); it does not toggle

aria: role="switch" on the native checkbox; checked state is exposed as aria-checked by the native input
aria-describedby -> description and error ids (same root)
required: native required; the asterisk is aria-hidden
error: sets a customError validity, so the form blocks submission
the thumb is aria-hidden; on/off is never conveyed by color alone (thumb position also changes)
announcements: error text is announced once when it appears (persistent aria-live=polite region)

useCases.when: A setting that is on or off and takes effect at once
The consequence of turning it on needs explaining
A setting must be on before the form can be sent
useCases.use: required with a label that states what is enabled

antiPatterns.pattern: A switch whose change is only recorded when the form is submitted
antiPatterns.why: A switch reads as an immediate setting; a deferred yes/no choice reads as a checkbox

antiPatterns.pattern: Choosing several options from a list, or exactly one
antiPatterns.why: Each switch is an independent setting

antiPatterns.pattern: A pressed-state button for a tool or a formatting option
antiPatterns.why: A switch is a form control with a name and a submitted value
The label is the only name for the switch
antiPatterns.alternative: A label that states what turns on

drift.contract: label, description and error are props of Switch
drift.realization: shadcn composes Field parts around Switch; shadow DOM requires them inside
shadcn default track is input at low contrast; changed for WCAG 1.4.11
not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset

openQuestions.question: Contract content drafted with the contract-author skill (visual reference, WAI-ARIA APG)?
openQuestions.answer: Yes: APG switch pattern, label row beside the track; sizes default and sm from the visual reference.

openQuestions.question: Native <input type=checkbox role=switch>, or a custom element with ARIA only?
openQuestions.answer: Native input with role=switch, like Checkbox: Space, focus, validity and label activation come for free. Chosen by the recommendation; no one was available to approve (SB-0011).

openQuestions.question: Is checked reflected to an attribute?
openQuestions.answer: No, same as Checkbox: the attribute is the default that form reset restores.

openQuestions.question: Is label required?
openQuestions.answer: Yes, like Checkbox and Input. hide-label keeps it as the accessible name.

openQuestions.question: Which sizes?
openQuestions.answer: default (32x20 track) and sm (24x16), the sizes the semantic tokens size.switch.* already define. Mapped through the registered size alias (default -> medium, sm -> small).

openQuestions.question: Does Enter toggle the switch?
openQuestions.answer: No. Space toggles (APG); Enter submits the form (SB-0009), as in Checkbox.

openQuestions.question: How does the 20px-high track meet WCAG 2.5.8 target size?
openQuestions.answer: The whole field row is the click target with a 24px minimum height (switch.min-height = size.control.xs), the label row exception used by Checkbox.

openQuestions.question: Is there a read-only or indeterminate state?
openQuestions.answer: No. Neither is native to a switch and the visual reference has none; add by a new decision if needed.
